historical_growth.notes: 5yr figures for revenue/equity/FCF are inflated by the 2021 Alexion acquisition (one-off step change in the balance sheet and revenue base), not organic growth -- the 10yr CAGRs are used as the more representative anchor and all three (revenue 9.1%, equity 10.2%, EPS 11.4%) cluster within 2.3pp of each other, well inside the 30% divergence threshold. Owner-FCF-adjusted (SBC-deducted) series used throughout: FY2019 $1,731m -> FY2025 $11,046m.

scenario_narratives.base: Oncology (Enhertu, Tagrisso, Imfinzi, Datroway) and Rare Disease (Alexion) growth offset the Farxiga US LOE and China VBP headwinds broadly as management has guided through H1 2026, with the late-stage pipeline (baxdrostat, elecoglipron) launching into cardiometabolic/obesity from FY2028; margins keep climbing toward a mature ~36% as Alexion synergies complete.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new cardiometabolic/obesity franchise and continued oncology expansion into earlier treatment lines drive above-guidance growth; the harmonised global listing supports a re-rating toward US pharma peer multiples.
scenario_narratives.bear: Farxiga LOE and expanding IRA price negotiation prove deeper than guided, China legal exposure escalates, and further late-stage pipeline failures (following FY2025's RESOLUTE/LATIFY misses) leave oncology/Rare Disease growth unable to fully offset the CVRM decline.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AstraZeneca is valued as a large, diversified, patent-protected biopharmaceutical company on a standard owner-FCF DCF. Owner FCF strips SBC (a modest, declining 1.2% of revenue for this filer) from reported FCF; interest income is NOT stripped because AstraZeneca carries net debt ($23.4bn), not net cash. The forward margin is built bottom-up from EBITDA, D&A, capex and cash tax components rather than carrying forward the FY2025 margin flat, because FY2025's reported figures embed one-off distortions (large non-cash intangible amortisation/impairment from serial M&A depressing reported D&A comparability, and an elevated capex ratio from the in-flight $50bn US manufacturing programme) that will not persist unchanged. The cash tax rate is anchored to management's own guided Core Tax Rate (18-22%) rather than the historical cash-tax/reported-PBT ratio, since reported PBT is itself depressed by the same non-cash M&A charges.
key_risks_to_valuation: Farxiga US loss of exclusivity (2026) plus IRA Medicare price negotiation expanding to additional blockbusters (Calquence from 2027) -- a visible, quantifiable, and possibly still-understated headwind to the CVRM franchise
Unresolved China legal/regulatory investigation (Leon Wang indictment) on AstraZeneca's second-largest single market, with a linked US securities investor lawsuit
Binary late-stage pipeline trial-failure risk given ~24%-of-revenue R&D intensity (FY2025's RESOLUTE and LATIFY misses demonstrate this is a live, recurring risk, not hypothetical)
Continued heavy bolt-on M&A and the $50bn US manufacturing commitment could keep capex elevated for longer than modeled, delaying the FCF margin's climb to maturity

FX exposure: USD-reporting UK-domiciled company with material non-US revenue (57% of FY2025 total) means currency swings materially affect reported (CER-adjusted) growth even though the model itself is built entirely in USD

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 146.66-212.71
data_sources.financials: AZN_Metrics.csv (metrics_normalized, FY2015-FY2025 annual + interims) and AZN_Annual_FY2025.txt (20-F/Annual Report) net debt reconciliation, Core-vs-Reported reconciliation, and cash flow statement
data_sources.qualitative: AZN_Analysis.json (2026-09-26), including FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at Q2 2026 results (26 July 2026)

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/20-F FY2025 cash flow statement (Share-based payments charge, Note 29, $719m). EquityAwardTaxes KPI is 0 across the full history for this filer; 'Own shares purchased by Employee Benefit Trust' ($521m FY2025) is the vesting-funding mechanism and is recorded as ShareRepurchases (buyback-equivalent), not a separate net-share-settlement withholding tax line -- UK/pharma filers do not disclose that split the way US tech 10-Ks do.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-denominated flows (AZN reports in USD despite UK domicile) discounted at a USD large-cap-pharma WACC: US 10yr risk-free ~4.2% + ERP ~5.0% x beta ~0.7 (defensive, low-cyclicality pharma) + a modest premium for elevated M&A-funded leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~1.2x) nets to ~7.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities ($1,803m, ~6% of total debt+leases) are immaterial to AZN's capital structure (dominated by $29.6bn of bonds/loans). Held inside net_debt per the company's own Net Debt definition (interest-bearing loans and borrowings + lease liabilities, net of cash); lease principal+interest are NOT separately stripped from FCF because they are already inside reported operating cash flow and 'Other capital expenditure' as per the company's own segment presentation -- deducting them again would double count on a line this small. This is the single lease treatment; not applying adaptation section 7 in full given immateriality, but flagging the choice explicitly.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are $52-85m against $48.7bn of equity (<0.2%) -- immaterial, not adjusted for.
inputs.notes: Model: standard owner-FCF DCF for a large, profitable, cash-generative global biopharma operating company (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table, row 1/2: 'Operating company... routes to Owner-FCF DCF'). Not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed shell. USD-reporting UK-domiciled filer, USD ADR->harmonised NYSE ordinary-share listing (Feb-2026) at 1-for-1 parity with the legacy ADR, so no currency mismatch: both price and financials are USD. Net debt company ($23.4bn) -- NOT net cash -- so interest income is NOT stripped from FCF per section 1(b) (that adjustment only applies when net cash > 1x FCF base). FY2025 owner FCF margin 18.8% (11,046/58,739), still climbing from ~7-8% in 2019-2020 as Alexion integration and oncology scale drive EBITDA margin from ~20% (2021) to 33% (2025) -- 10-year explicit horizon used per section 2(d) since margin has not fully matured. Cash tax rate anchored to management's own guided Core Tax Rate (18-22% FY2026) rather than the historical cash-tax/PBT ratio (23-32%), because reported PBT is depressed by large non-cash intangible amortisation/impairment from serial M&A (Alexion, CinCor) -- charging a tax rate derived from that distorted PBT against a 'clean' EBITDA-based EBIT would overstate the tax charge. D&A% blends toward a level below the raw FY2025 reported figure (9.8% of revenue) for the same reason: reported D&A includes lumpy impairment charges (e.g. $4.3bn intangible amortisation/impairment excluded from Core operating profit in FY2025) that are not a steady-state run-rate. Capex% (PP&E + intangibles, both organic and bolt-on business-development spend) is elevated in the near term (8.2% FY2023 -> 10.1% FY2025) reflecting the $50bn US manufacturing/R&D investment programme through 2030 and continued bolt-on M&A (EsoBiotec, SixPeaks, Modella AI, CinCor), tapering toward a more moderate maintenance level in the back half of the explicit horizon. Historical growth: 10yr equity CAGR 10.2% selected as the primary anchor (vs 10yr revenue CAGR 9.1%, EPS CAGR 11.4%) -- all three cluster within ~2pp, no divergence flag needed; the 5yr figures (equity 25.5%, revenue 17.2%) are distorted by the 2021 Alexion acquisition (a one-off equity/balance-sheet step-change) and are not used as the anchor.

bear.narrative: Bear case: Farxiga's US LOE proves deeper and more prolonged than guided, compounded by IRA Medicare price negotiation expanding beyond Farxiga (round one) and Calquence (round two, effective 2027) to touch additional blockbusters, and the unresolved China legal exposure (Leon Wang indictment, medical insurance fraud/data charges) escalates into material fines, license restrictions or further securities litigation given China is AstraZeneca's second-largest single market. Pipeline setbacks recur (as with FY2025's RESOLUTE and LATIFY Phase III misses) and the ~24%-of-revenue R&D intensity produces a run of costly late-stage failures without a commensurate string of successes, so oncology/Rare Disease growth only partially offsets the CVRM decline. Margins stay near current levels as the $50bn US manufacturing commitment and continued bolt-on M&A keep capex and integration costs elevated without full payoff.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2026 growth held near management's own reconfirmed guidance (mid-to-high single-digit Total Revenue, low-double-digit Core EPS at CER) despite the visible Farxiga US LOE and China VBP headwinds, because oncology (Enhertu, Tagrisso, Datroway) and Rare Disease (Alexion) continue offsetting the CVRM decline as management has stated through H1 2026. Growth stays in the mid-single digits through the back half of the explicit window as the late-stage pipeline (baxdrostat, elecoglipron, gefurulimab) launches into cardiometabolic and rare disease, then decelerates to a 3% terminal rate as the industry's structural ~7% healthcare-spend growth is tempered by IRA price-negotiation pressure expanding beyond Farxiga/Calquence. EBITDA margin continues its multi-year climb (20%->33% since 2021) toward a mature ~36% as Alexion integration synergies complete and oncology mix (higher-margin, patent-protected) keeps rising, but the ramp is capped well below best-in-class large-pharma peers given AstraZeneca's persistently high R&D intensity (~24% of revenue) and the $50bn US manufacturing capex programme running through 2030.

bull.narrative: Bull case: the oncology and cardiometabolic pipeline delivers -- baxdrostat and the oral GLP-1/amylin franchise (elecoglipron, AZD6234) succeed in Phase III and capture meaningful share of a large new hypertension/obesity market, Enhertu/Datroway expand into earlier lines of treatment faster than modeled, and emerging-markets ex-China growth (19-22% in FY2025) continues to more than offset Farxiga LOE and the China legal overhang. The harmonised NYSE/LSE/Stockholm listing broadens the investor base and supports a re-rating toward US large-pharma peer multiples. Margins expand further as Alexion synergies complete and the US manufacturing investment locks in the negotiated tariff exemption without further capital escalation.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default shifted slightly toward bear (20% vs default 15%) given two concrete, already-visible headwinds rather than hypothetical risks: the Farxiga US LOE is showing up in reported CVRM declines now, and the China legal exposure (Leon Wang indictment) is an active, unresolved investigation on AstraZeneca's second-largest single market with a linked US securities suit. Bull trimmed to 25% (vs default 35%) because the bull case requires several independent pipeline wins (baxdrostat, elecoglipron/AZD5004, gefurulimab) to read through commercially, on top of already-strong execution -- multiple things must go right, not one. Base carries the plurality reflecting a going, well-diversified, patent-protected large-pharma franchise with a genuinely deep late-stage pipeline (100+ Phase III studies) that management has a strong track record of executing.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
